claims.description: Winning tickets learn faster: at Pm=21.1% the early-stopping iteration (minimum validation loss) occurs 38% earlier than for the unpruned network.
Test accuracy at early stop improves by more than 0.3 percentage points at Pm=13.5% relative to the unpruned network.
By Pm=3.6% the accuracy gain is gone: test accuracy returns to the level of the original unpruned network.
The original initialisation matters: at Pm=21% the winning ticket reaches minimum validation loss 2.51x faster than the same mask with a resampled initialisation.
At Pm=21% the winning ticket is about half a percentage point more accurate than the same mask randomly reinitialised.
Winning tickets generalise better, not just optimise faster: at iteration 50,000 they still improve test accuracy by up to 0.35 percentage points over the unpruned network.

Structural check of the pruning schedule: pruning 20% of surviving weights per round in each fully-connected layer and 10% in the output layer, layer-wise, leaves Pm=21.1% of the 266,200 weights after 7 rounds.
